revisedDocket.title: Stock launchers: may a printed Payload define the ammunition pool when no launcher count is printed?
evidence: Published: a standard proton torpedo launcher holds three torpedoes; concussion launcher capacity is light 6 / medium 16 / heavy 30 (Starships of the Galaxy, Launchers entries, pp.45-46). These are properties of a LAUNCHER.
Published: the statblock Payload line is the vehicle's complement of grenades, rockets, missiles and torpedoes (Core Rulebook statblock key). It is a carried complement.

Of the 64 groups, 60 attack lines name only the ammunition ("proton torpedoes +14"), 2 use a singular launcher noun and 2 a plural without a number; no statblock text shows a launcher count (58 located, 0 numeric).
Payload is corroborated in the text for 54 groups (3 inside a multi-ammunition line); 3 show no payload line, 1 a different figure and 6 could not be located (all 10 need the PDF).
resolvedBySourceResearch: 3 groups carry a printed hardwareCount in the record but are named by their ammunition, so the gate does not read it as a launcher count: the PDF decides what that figure counts (3 would run if it is a launcher count and nothing else blocks them).
14 groups have a launcher count nobody has reviewed (record value null, not "silent"): a PDF check may find a count (13 would run) or confirm silence.
genuinelySilent: 47 groups: the record certifies the source silent on the launcher count and the text corroborates it. 41 of them have no other blocker.
needsRuling: Only the genuinely silent groups: whether the Payload alone may define the pool.

options.text: Project convention STOCK_POOL: the printed Payload is the pool (no magazine, no reload) for stock groups whose launcher count the source does not print. Executes, but is labelled a project convention, never canonical.
Keep requiring a launcher count (source-printed or GM-certified). No change; these groups stay GM-configured.
Both: canonical where a count is printed after the PDF check, STOCK_POOL convention where the source is silent, GM configuration otherwise.

unlock.note: canonical share = the two source-research rows above; convention share = the silent row

revisedDocket.consequences: Option 1 changes what "executable" means for ammunition (launched rounds are drawn from the Payload with no per-launcher magazine); installed launchers are unaffected. It must be reported as its own outcome so canonical coverage is not inflated.
revisedDocket.recommendation: UNAPPROVED, evidence-based: option 3, with a distinct STOCK_POOL_CONVENTION outcome. The text shows the book defines Payload as a carried complement and capacity as a launcher property, so the Payload alone does not establish a launcher count; do the PDF check on the 17 unreviewed or numeric-count groups first.

revisedDocket.title: Weapons whose type has no Table 10-2 row: how is range resolved?
evidence: Core Rulebook, Attack with Vehicle Weapon: "The maximum range and the range modifiers of a vehicle weapon depend on the weapon used (see Table 10-2: Vehicle Weapon Ranges)." The table itself is an image and is not in the text corpus; data/vehicle-weapon-ranges.json holds its 9 rows.
46 groups on 39 vehicles name weapons that match none of those rows (41 distinct designations; 7 have no other blocker). Statblocks located in the text: 33.
resolvedBySourceResearch: None resolvable from text: whether the PDF table or the weapon entries give these weapons a range cannot be read from the OCR corpus.
genuinelySilent: Not established. The owner (or a session with the PDFs) must read Table 10-2 and each weapon entry before any group is called silent.
needsRuling: Only the weapons the PDF shows have no range at all.

options.text: Keep refusing groups with no printed range row.
GM-certified range bands per weapon, labelled GM_CONFIGURED.
Owner-supplied mapping of each type to an existing row, labelled project convention.

revisedDocket.consequences: Options 2 and 3 only make the range lookup resolve; 39 of the 46 groups also carry other blockers.
revisedDocket.recommendation: UNAPPROVED: do not rule yet. Read Table 10-2 and the listed weapon entries in the PDF first (checklist below); then decide only for weapons the book leaves without a range.

revisedDocket.title: Printed attack totals that the Core formula plus battery assistance does not reproduce
evidence: Core vehicle attack basis used by the gate: crew Base Attack + Intelligence modifier, +2 for a pilot-crewed weapon, +2 per assisting gunner of a printed battery (Core pp.170-171).

Of 29 groups on 10 capital ships, 14 are reproduced exactly (residual 0) once the Base Atk / Int shown in the statblock text replace the record's values: the RECORD disagrees with the text on 3 vehicles. That is an extraction defect, not a rules gap.

15 groups remain unexplained with the text values (residuals 1:3, 2:2, 4:1, -4:1, -2:2, -8:1, -1:4, -3:1); the residual equals the Core crew-quality attack bonus in 0 of them, so crew quality does not explain them either.
A wider scan of 319 located statblocks finds the record's Base Atk differing from the text on 8 vehicles and Int on 10.
resolvedBySourceResearch: 14 groups, if the PDF confirms the text Base Atk / Int (10 would then run with no other blocker).
genuinelySilent: Not applicable: these are printed figures, not omissions.
needsRuling: 15 groups whose printed total stays unexplained after the correction (8 would run with no other blocker), plus the Eclipse's conflicting +7 header / +15 row.

options.text: Accept the verified printed total as the published generic-crew modifier and record the unexplained residual (labelled "printed-authority", not "reconciled"). It does not transfer to assigned characters, whose modifier is computed from their own Base Attack and Intelligence.

revisedDocket.consequences: Option 2 makes the book's number authoritative without an explaining rule; it must stay labelled so a later rule can replace it.
revisedDocket.recommendation: UNAPPROVED: first correct the record Base Atk / Int from the PDF (no ruling needed); only then decide option 2 for the remaining residuals.

revisedDocket.title: Qualitative firing arcs
evidence: 5 groups state an arc without a geometry: Scurrg H-6 Prototype Bomber - "SOURCE_SILENT_CONFIRMED"; Eclipse - "axial keel mounted, whole-ship alignment"; Koensayr Manufacturing BTL-58 K-wing - "second generation forward turret; first-generation relationship unspecified"; MandalMotors StarViper Assault Fighter - "articulated broad field, exact arc not quantified"; Rendili Star Drive Light Corvette - "flank-mounted turrets; numeric/coverage arcs not printed".
V-P6C-01 (existing owner ruling): a defined fixed-forward arc is enforced; a confirmed-silent arc imposes no restriction; a stated but uninterpretable arc is refused.
resolvedBySourceResearch: None: the wording is the source wording.
genuinelySilent: The geometry (degrees, coverage) is not printed for any of the five.
needsRuling: All 5: how a stated-but-undefined arc is treated.

options.text: GM-certified arc per group, labelled GM_CONFIGURED (the stated direction recorded beside it).
Treat an undefined arc as unrestricted (this would let a "forward-mounted" weapon fire anywhere).

revisedDocket.consequences: Option 3 contradicts the stated direction; option 2 keeps GM adjudication but is not canonical.
revisedDocket.recommendation: UNAPPROVED: option 2 (GM-certified arcs), as you suggested; option 3 is not recommended.

revisedDocket.title: Special-effect devices without ordinary damage
evidence: All 6 groups print a weapon entry in the statblock text: harpoon gun, boarding drill, microtractor-pressor, gravity mine, marker missile, plasma beam cutter.

4 use the tractor-beam notation "Atk +N, Dmg - (grapple +M)" (boarding drill, microtractor-pressor, plasma beam cutter and the harpoon gun's grapple +27), which is the notation the existing tractor-beam opposed-control mechanic already reads for tractor beams.

The marker missile prints "target vessel successfully tagged for tracking" and the gravity mine refers to a sidebar; the Droch boarding drill prints a full procedure (standard action, adjacent square, attaches to the target).
resolvedBySourceResearch: The effect text for each is printed (not silent); extracting it is source work, not a ruling.
genuinelySilent: Gravity mine effect lives in a sidebar not captured here; the harpoon gun has no located statblock detail.
needsRuling: Whether a grapple-notation device should reuse the tractor-beam opposed-control mechanic (a mechanic choice), and whether narrative-only effects (marker missile tagging) are certified manual.

options.text: Leave as implementation-required until each effect is specified from its printed text.
Reuse the tractor-beam opposed-control mechanic for grapple-notation devices (owner confirms it is the right generic mechanic) and certify narrative-only devices as GM_ADJUDICATED.

revisedDocket.consequences: Option 2 changes reporting only for GM_ADJUDICATED devices (neither executable nor failed); the grapple devices become implementation work with a printed basis.
revisedDocket.recommendation: UNAPPROVED: separate the two kinds as you suggested; ask for the ruling only on the reuse of the tractor-beam mechanic after the printed text of each device is read.
